Xin Li李鑫

I work on LLM agents — evaluating what they can do, training them, and orchestrating them with tools, verifiers and each other to get real tasks done. Lately, on agents that improve themselves.

Change the future

The research, as one loopclockwise from 01

01

Evaluate

What can a model really do, and where does it fail — and does the score mean what it appears to mean?

  • WirelessMathBench-XL
  • DafnyComp
  • LiveCANNBench
  • RobustMAD
  • WirelessMathBench

02

Train

What should a model be rewarded for — especially when there is no answer key?

  • DN-MOPD
  • Re:Form
  • GraphReduce

03

Orchestrate

What should a trained model be wrapped in — tools, checks, retries, other agents — for the task to actually get done, without breaking what already worked?

  • DebateLedger
  • TLVC
  • LACP

03 → 01. Every new way of orchestrating models creates new failure modes, which need to be evaluated in turn.

So far, mostly where an answer can be checked:formal verificationmathematicscodeNow, self-improvement where it can't.

RecentAll news →

  1. Sep 2026Our paper SIM-D2NN (on onboard terrain classification straight from raw SAR data, using a stacked metasurface as the classifier) was accepted to IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing.
  2. Sep 2026Two of our papers were accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track: WirelessMathBench-XL, a wireless-math benchmark shipped with a rerunnable contamination audit, and DebateLedger, a protocol separating harmful collapse from useful correction in multi-agent LLM debate.
  3. Aug 2026Two of our papers were accepted to EMNLP 2026: TLVC, on picking the right verifier for best-of-K reasoning selection (Findings), and GraphReduce, on coverage-preserving LLM aggregation of e-commerce reviews (Industry Track).
  4. Jun 2026Our paper RobustMAD (a robustness benchmark for multimodal small language models in anomaly detection) was accepted to TMLR.
  5. May 2026Our paper Re:Form (on cutting human priors from RL-trained formal software verification) was accepted to TMLR.

Before the Ph.D.

Robot perception — visual-inertial odometry at MEGVII, RGB-D + IMU indoor mapping at Microsoft Research Asia, and multimodal localization at Gausium Robotics, where I led a five-engineer team and shipped to a fleet of 1,000+ commercial cleaning robots. More →
